[[File:Crystal structure.png|thumbnail|400px]]
'''Crystal''' is a solid with periodic atomic structure.

== Classification ==

=== Grain ===

==== Single crystal ====

An ideal single crystal consists of cells of atoms that repeat over the entire volume of the solid.

It is said to be perfectly '''translationally symmetric'''.

==== Polycrystalline ====
[[File:Galvanised steel plate.png|thumbnail|right|In galvanised steel, the grains are large enough to be seen with the naked eye, which is not the case for most polycrystals.]]
[[File:Hypoeutectoid iron-carbon alloy.png|thumbnail|left|In most polycrystals, the grains are of [[microscopic scale]].]]
A polycrystalline has multiple '''grains''', each similar to a single crystal.

The boundaries between two grains are called '''grain boundaries'''.

Most crystals on the [[macroscopic scale]] are polycrystalline, and the most polycrystal grains are '''polyhedrals''' with $120^\circ$ angle between surfaces, as grain boundaries are high energy surfaces that tend to naturally minimise themselves.

== Atomic structure ==

=== Unit cell and lattice system ===

The geometry of the smallest repeating unit of a crystal, called a '''unit cell''', can be modelled by 14 '''Bravais lattices''', classed into 7 families.<ref>{{#cite:Q4223}}</ref>

=== Defect ===

[[File:CrystalGrainGrowth.mp4|The cross sections of polycrystals can be simulated by dropping small balls dropped in a single layer between two transparent glasses, as seen, the structure is not perfectly translationally symmetric even within the same grain due to presence of '''defects'''.|thumbnail]]
Most real-world crystals are '''imperfect''', i.e., their structures do not perfectly follow the lattice model.

e.g,

* there may be atoms missing completely, a phenomenon known as '''vacancy''';
* or some atoms maybe found away from their expected place, a phenomenon known as '''dislocation'''.

<ref>{{#cite:Q4205}}</ref>

==== Significance of defects ====

Defects have an impact on

* Mechanical strength
* Rate of atomic diffusion

<ref>{{#cite:Q4205}}</ref>
